title: Direct-mapped: miss then hit
description: See how an address is split into *tag*, *index* and *offset*, why the first load of a line *misses*, and why its neighbour then *hits*.

steps.text: This cache has 8 sets and 16-byte lines. So every address is cut in three: the low 4 bits are the *offset* (which byte of the line), the next 3 are the *index* (which set), and the other 5 are the *tag*.
Load from `0x0A4`. Type it in the address box and press Issue.
steps.hint: The address box is next to the Issue button. Type `0x0A4` there.

steps.text: That load missed: the cache had nothing yet. Drag the timeline back to step 1.2, the *tag compare*, to see it happen.
Now type `0x0A8` in the address box, but do not issue it. Compare its tag, index and offset in the strip with those of `0x0A4`.
You are about to load `0x0A8`. Will it hit or miss?
options: Hit: it is in the same line as `0x0A4`
Miss: it is a different address
steps.explain: A hit. A miss brings in the whole 16-byte line, `0x0A0` to `0x0AF`, and `0x0A8` is in it. Only the *offset* differs.
steps.hint: Compare the tag and the index of `0x0A8` with those of `0x0A4` in the strip.
Type `0x0A8` in the address box and press Issue.

steps.text: A hit. The line was already in set 2, so the table did not change. Only the counters and `r1` did.
